claim: Ki-67 and RepoMan have key roles during mitotic exit.
source: Ki-67 and RepoMan have key roles during mitotic exit.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact and is supported by the citation of previous work (Booth et al., 2014).

claim: Ki-67 organizes the mitotic chromosome periphery.
source: Previously, we showed that Ki-67 organizes the mitotic chromosome periphery and recruits protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to chromatin at anaphase onset, in a similar manner as RepoMan (Booth et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Booth et al., 2014).

claim: Ki-67 recruits protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to chromatin at anaphase onset.
source: Previously, we showed that Ki-67 organizes the mitotic chromosome periphery and recruits protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to chromatin at anaphase onset, in a similar manner as RepoMan (Booth et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Booth et al., 2014).

claim: RepoMan recruits PP1 to chromatin at anaphase onset in a similar manner as Ki-67.
source: Previously, we showed that Ki-67 organizes the mitotic chromosome periphery and recruits protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to chromatin at anaphase onset, in a similar manner as RepoMan (Booth et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Booth et al., 2014).

claim: Ki-67 and RepoMan bind PP1 using an identical, yet novel mechanism.
source: Unexpectedly, our data also reveal that Ki-67 and RepoMan bind PP1 using an identical, yet novel mechanism, interacting with a PP1 pocket that is engaged only by these two PP1 regulators.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural and biochemical data presented in the manuscript, including crystal structures and ITC measurements.

claim: Ki-67 and RepoMan interact with a PP1 pocket that is engaged only by these two PP1 regulators.
source: Unexpectedly, our data also reveal that Ki-67 and RepoMan bind PP1 using an identical, yet novel mechanism, interacting with a PP1 pocket that is engaged only by these two PP1 regulators.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data and database searches showing that only Ki-67 and RepoMan contain the KiR-SLiM motif.

claim: The assembly of Ki-67:PP1 and RepoMan:PP1 holoenzymes is dynamically regulated by Aurora B kinase during mitosis.
source: Here we show how Ki-67 and RepoMan form mitotic exit phosphatases by recruiting PP1, how they distinguish between distinct PP1 isoforms and how the assembly of these two holoenzymes are dynamically regulated by Aurora B kinase during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro phosphorylation assays, NMR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and ITC measurements showing that Aurora B phosphorylation weakens PP1 binding.

claim: Mitotic exit comprises a complex series of events that includes sister chromatid segregation, mitotic spindle disassembly, nuclear-envelope re-assembly and chromosome decondensation.
source: Mitotic exit comprises a complex series of events that includes sister chromatid segregation, mitotic spindle disassembly, nuclear-envelope re-assembly and chromosome decondensation (Wurzenberger and Gerlich, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established literature (Wurzenberger and Gerlich, 2011).

claim: Exiting mitosis requires the specific engagement and activation of protein phosphatases, including ser/thr phosphatase protein phosphatase 1 (PP1).
source: The emerging picture is that exiting mitosis requires the specific engagement and activation of protein phosphatases, including ser/thr phosphatase protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) (Funabiki and Wynne, 2013; Rosenberg et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Funabiki and Wynne, 2013; Rosenberg et al., 2011).

claim: PP1 exhibits broad specificity but acts in a highly specific manner by forming stable complexes, known as holoenzymes, with regulatory proteins.
source: While PP1 exhibits broad specificity, it acts in a highly specific manner by forming stable complexes, known as holoenzymes, with a host of regulatory proteins that direct PP1 activity towards specific substrates and localize PP1 to specific regions of the cell (Hendrickx et al., 2009; Bollen et al., 2010; Peti et al., 2013; Peti and Page, 2015; Choy et al., 2014; O'Connell et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established literature (Hendrickx et al., 2009; Bollen et al., 2010; Peti et al., 2013; Peti and Page, 2015; Choy et al., 2014; O'Connell et al., 2012).

claim: Ki-67 is widely used as a prognostic marker for many cancers.
source: Ki-67 is widely used as a prognostic marker for many cancers (Dowsett et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2016; Sobecki et al., 2016), yet for decades, its molecular function remained largely unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical literature (Dowsett et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2016; Sobecki et al., 2016).

claim: One role of Ki-67 is to function as a 'DNA surfactant', preventing individual chromosomes from collapsing into a single chromatin mass upon nuclear envelope disassembly by binding directly to the surface of chromatin.
source: Recently, it was shown that one role of Ki-67 is to function as a 'DNA surfactant', preventing individual chromosomes from collapsing into a single chromatin mass upon nuclear envelope disassembly by binding directly to the surface of chromatin (Cuylen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent research (Cuylen et al., 2016).

claim: Ki-67 binds and regulates the activity of PP1 during mitosis using the canonical PP1 RVxF small linear motif (SLiM).
source: A second recently discovered function is that it binds and regulates the activity of PP1 during mitosis using the canonical PP1 RVxF small linear motif (SLiM) (Booth et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Booth et al., 2014).

claim: The only other protein that exhibits any sequence similarity with Ki-67 near its RVxF motif is RepoMan.
source: The only other protein that exhibits any sequence similarity with Ki-67 near its RVxF motif is RepoMan (recruits PP1γ onto mitotic chromatin at anaphase, also known as cell division cycle associated 2, CDCA2), a nuclear-specific protein that was discovered for its ability to specifically recruit PP1γ to chromosomes at anaphase onset and, like Ki-67, is upregulated in many cancers (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis and citations to previous research (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli, 2014).

claim: RepoMan is upregulated in many cancers.
source: The only other protein that exhibits any sequence similarity with Ki-67 near its RVxF motif is RepoMan (recruits PP1γ onto mitotic chromatin at anaphase, also known as cell division cycle associated 2, CDCA2), a nuclear-specific protein that was discovered for its ability to specifically recruit PP1γ to chromosomes at anaphase onset and, like Ki-67, is upregulated in many cancers (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli, 2014).

claim: PP1γ is essential for histone dephosphorylation, nuclear-envelope reassembly and chromatin remodeling during mitotic exit.
source: During mitotic exit, PP1, in particular PP1γ (PP1 isoforms include PP1α, PP1β, PP1γ and PP1γ2; ≥ 85% identity between isoforms), is essential for histone dephosphorylation, nuclear-envelope reassembly and chromatin remodeling (Qian et al., 2011; Vagnarelli et al., 2006; Wurzenberger et al., 2012; Qian et al., 2013; Vagnarelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research (Qian et al., 2011; Vagnarelli et al., 2006; Wurzenberger et al., 2012; Qian et al., 2013; Vagnarelli et al., 2011).

claim: PP1 isoforms include PP1α, PP1β, PP1γ and PP1γ2 with ≥ 85% identity between isoforms.
source: During mitotic exit, PP1, in particular PP1γ (PP1 isoforms include PP1α, PP1β, PP1γ and PP1γ2; ≥ 85% identity between isoforms), is essential for histone dephosphorylation, nuclear-envelope reassembly and chromatin remodeling (Qian et al., 2011; Vagnarelli et al., 2006; Wurzenberger et al., 2012; Qian et al., 2013; Vagnarelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PP1 isoforms.

claim: PP1γ-specific processes during mitotic exit are mediated largely by the Ki-67:PP1γ and RepoMan:PP1γ holoenzymes.
source: These PP1γ-specific processes are mediated largely by the Ki-67:PP1γ and RepoMan:PP1γ holoenzymes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the previous statements and supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ki-67496-536 and RepoMan383-423 bind PP1γ7–323 with a 1:1 stoichiometry.
source: Using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), we showed that Ki-67496-536 and RepoMan383-423 bind PP1γ7–323 with a 1:1 stoichiometry and with nearly equivalent affinities (Figure 1B, left; Figure 1—figure supplement 1; KD = 193 ± 16 nM and 133 ± 5 nM; respectively; all ITC experiments are summarized in Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Table 1.

claim: Ki-67496-536 binds PP1γ7–323 with a KD of 193 ± 16 nM.
source: Using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), we showed that Ki-67496-536 and RepoMan383-423 bind PP1γ7–323 with a 1:1 stoichiometry and with nearly equivalent affinities (Figure 1B, left; Figure 1—figure supplement 1; KD = 193 ± 16 nM and 133 ± 5 nM; respectively; all ITC experiments are summarized in Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Table 1.

claim: RepoMan383-423 binds PP1γ7–323 with a KD of 133 ± 5 nM.
source: Using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), we showed that Ki-67496-536 and RepoMan383-423 bind PP1γ7–323 with a 1:1 stoichiometry and with nearly equivalent affinities (Figure 1B, left; Figure 1—figure supplement 1; KD = 193 ± 16 nM and 133 ± 5 nM; respectively; all ITC experiments are summarized in Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Table 1.

claim: Extending the Ki-67/RepoMan PP1-binding domain beyond residues 496-536/383-423 does not enhance binding to PP1.
source: We also showed that extending this domain does not enhance binding (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1.

claim: All residues in the conserved region of RepoMan (383-423) interact with PP1.
source: Finally, NMR spectroscopy experiments with RepoMan confirmed that all residues in this conserved region interact with PP1 (Figure 1—figure supplements 2,3).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: The crystal structure of the Ki-67:PP1γ holoenzyme was determined to 2.0 Å resolution.
source: To identify this mechanism, we determined the crystal structures of the Ki-67496-536:PP1γ7–308 and RepoMan383-423:PP1γ7–308 holoenzymes complexes to 2.0 Å and 1.3 Å, respectively (Figure 1C,D; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data presented in Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: The crystal structure of the RepoMan:PP1γ holoenzyme was determined to 1.3 Å resolution.
source: To identify this mechanism, we determined the crystal structures of the Ki-67496-536:PP1γ7–308 and RepoMan383-423:PP1γ7–308 holoenzymes complexes to 2.0 Å and 1.3 Å, respectively (Figure 1C,D; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data presented in Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Ki-67 and RepoMan form a classical β-hairpin on the top of PP1 that extends from the PP1 RVxF binding pocket towards the PP1 N-terminus and then back again.
source: Namely, Ki-67 and RepoMan form a classical β-hairpin on the top of PP1 that extends from the PP1 RVxF binding pocket towards the PP1 N-terminus and then back again (Figure 1D; ~2600 Å of buried surface area).
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The Ki-67/RepoMan:PP1 interaction buries approximately 2600 Å² of surface area.
source: Namely, Ki-67 and RepoMan form a classical β-hairpin on the top of PP1 that extends from the PP1 RVxF binding pocket towards the PP1 N-terminus and then back again (Figure 1D; ~2600 Å of buried surface area).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: Ki-67 and RepoMan bind PP1 using the RVxF-SLiM (505RVSF508Ki-67/392RVTF395RM) in the RVxF binding pocket.
source: The structures also show that two established PP1-specific SLiMs—the RVxF-SLiM (Egloff et al., 1997), 505RVSF508Ki-67/392RVTF395RM and the ΦΦ-SLiM (O'Connell et al., 2012), 515EL516Ki-67/402EV403RM —bind directly to PP1 in the RVxF and ΦΦ binding pockets (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 1D and citations to previous work (Egloff et al., 1997).

claim: Ki-67 and RepoMan bind PP1 using the ΦΦ-SLiM (515EL516Ki-67/402EV403RM) in the ΦΦ binding pocket.
source: The structures also show that two established PP1-specific SLiMs—the RVxF-SLiM (Egloff et al., 1997), 505RVSF508Ki-67/392RVTF395RM and the ΦΦ-SLiM (O'Connell et al., 2012), 515EL516Ki-67/402EV403RM —bind directly to PP1 in the RVxF and ΦΦ binding pockets (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 1D and citations to previous work (O'Connell et al., 2012).

claim: Ki-67/RepoMan residues C-terminal to the RVxF and ΦΦ SLiMs (aa 517–535/404–422) bind PP1 in a manner never observed for any other PP1 regulator.
source: However, as predicted, the Ki-67/RepoMan residues C-terminal to these SLiMs (aa 517–535/404–422) also bind PP1 and do so in a manner never observed for any other PP1 regulator (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 1D,E and comparison with other known PP1 regulator structures.

claim: Residues F517Ki-67/F404RM and P523Ki-67/A410RM are anchored to PP1γ via two hydrophobic pockets.
source: Residues F517Ki-67/F404RM and P523Ki-67/A410RM are anchored to PP1γ via two hydrophobic pockets while multiple residues in Ki-67/RepoMan bind the side chains of R74PP1, Y78PP1 and Q294PP1 via polar and salt bridge interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Multiple residues in Ki-67/RepoMan bind the side chains of R74PP1, Y78PP1 and Q294PP1 via polar and salt bridge interactions.
source: Residues F517Ki-67/F404RM and P523Ki-67/A410RM are anchored to PP1γ via two hydrophobic pockets while multiple residues in Ki-67/RepoMan bind the side chains of R74PP1, Y78PP1 and Q294PP1 via polar and salt bridge interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The Ki-67/RepoMan interaction orders PP1γ loop 1 (L1).
source: This orders PP1γ L1 (Figure 1C), a loop that is generally more dynamic in most free PP1 and PP1 holoenzyme structures as evidenced by its higher B-factors and less well-defined electron density.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 1C and comparison with other PP1 structures.

claim: Removing the KiR-SLiM residues (404-422) from RepoMan decreases the affinity for PP1 approximately five-fold.
source: Because these residues are critical for binding (removing them decreases the affinity ~five-fold; Figure 1B, right), we termed this novel PP1 interaction SLiM the KiR-SLiM (Ki-67-RepoMan SLiM).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 1B (right panel) comparing RepoMan383-423 (KD = 133 nM) with RepoMan383-404 (KD = 661 nM).

claim: The general KiR-SLiM motif is FDxxLP(P/A)N(T/S)PL(R/K)(R/K)Gx(T/S)P.
source: The general KiR-SLiM motif, FDxxLP(P/A)N(T/S)PL(R/K)(R/K)Gx(T/S)P was determined using HMMER (Figure 1F) (Finn et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by HMMER analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: A search of the UniProtK/Swiss-Prot database using the KiR-SLiM identified only Ki-67 and RepoMan proteins.
source: Critically, a subsequent search of the UniProtK/Swiss-Prot database (de Castro et al., 2006) using the most degenerate version of the KiR-SLiM identified only Ki-67 and RepoMan proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by database search results using ScanProsite.

claim: Only Ki-67 and RepoMan likely use the KiR-SLiM interaction surface on PP1.
source: This demonstrates that, unexpectedly, only these two PP1 regulators likely use the KiR-SLiM interaction surface on PP1.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the database search results showing that only Ki-67 and RepoMan contain the KiR-SLiM motif.

claim: In vivo, Ki-67 and RepoMan bind specifically to the β- and γ-isoforms, but not the α-isoform, of PP1.
source: In vivo, Ki-67 and RepoMan bind specifically to the β- and γ-isoforms, but not the α-isoform, of PP1 (Booth et al., 2014; Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Booth et al., 2014; Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli et al., 2011).

claim: PP1γ is recruited more efficiently than PP1β by Ki-67 and RepoMan.
source: As PP1γ is recruited more efficiently than PP1β (Booth et al., 2014), we focused our study on the PP1α and PP1γ isoforms.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Booth et al., 2014).

claim: The affinity of both Ki-67496-536 and RepoMan383-423 for PP1α7–330 is approximately four–six-fold weaker than for PP1γ7–323.
source: We confirmed this in vitro using ITC, which showed that the affinity of both Ki-67496-536 and RepoMan383-423 for PP1α7–330 is ~four–six-fold weaker than for PP1γ7–323 (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Deleting the last 15 residues of PP1γ has no impact on Ki-67/RepoMan binding.
source: To elucidate the molecular basis of isoform selectivity, we first tested the role of the PP1γ C-terminal residues. Deleting the last 15 residues of PP1γ had no impact on binding (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 comparing PP1γ7-323 and PP1γ7-308.

claim: The RepoMan383-441:PP1α7–300 holoenzyme structure is identical to the RepoMan:PP1γ structure (backbone RMSD = 0.22 Å).
source: We then tested if RepoMan binds PP1α differently by determining the structure of the RepoMan383-441:PP1α7–300 holoenzyme (2.6 Å; Figure 1—source data 1). The structures are identical (backbone RMSD = 0.22 Å), demonstrating that the isoform selectivity is due to one or more of the six amino acid differences in the PP1 catalytic domain (residues 7–300).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and structural comparison.

claim: The isoform selectivity of Ki-67/RepoMan for PP1γ over PP1α is due to one or more of the six amino acid differences in the PP1 catalytic domain (residues 7–300).
source: The structures are identical (backbone RMSD = 0.22 Å), demonstrating that the isoform selectivity is due to one or more of the six amino acid differences in the PP1 catalytic domain (residues 7–300).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural comparison showing identical binding modes despite different affinities.

claim: The PP1γR20Q mutation causes a ten-fold weaker binding to Ki-67 (KD = 2239 ± 124 nM).
source: The change of only a single amino acid, R20/Q20, switches PP1γ into a 'PP1α'-like isoform (PP1γR20Q; KD = 2239 ± 124 nM; ten fold weaker binding) and PP1α into a 'PP1γ'-like isoform (PP1αQ20R; KD = 199 ± 46 nM; similar binding to that of PP1γ).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 2B and Table 1.

claim: The PP1αQ20R mutation results in binding affinity similar to PP1γ (KD = 199 ± 46 nM).
source: The change of only a single amino acid, R20/Q20, switches PP1γ into a 'PP1α'-like isoform (PP1γR20Q; KD = 2239 ± 124 nM; ten fold weaker binding) and PP1α into a 'PP1γ'-like isoform (PP1αQ20R; KD = 199 ± 46 nM; similar binding to that of PP1γ).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 2B and Table 1.

claim: R20 confers isoform selectivity through its interactions with PP1 which order the L1 loop.
source: Although R20 does not interact with Ki-67 or RepoMan directly, it confers selectively through its interactions with PP1 which order the L1 loop.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural data showing R20 interactions with PP1 residues.

claim: The Arg20 sidechain forms a salt bridge with PP1 residue Glu77 and makes a planar stacking interaction (cation/π interaction) with Phe81.
source: Namely, the Arg20 sidechain forms a salt bridge with PP1 residue Glu77 and makes a planar stacking interaction (cation/π interaction) with Phe81.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Neither salt bridge nor cation/π interaction is possible with Q20, as the side chain is both uncharged and too short.
source: Neither interaction is possible with Q20, as the side chain is both uncharged and too short.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the chemical properties of glutamine compared to arginine.

claim: Only in PP1γ is the L1 loop pocket ordered and readily available for binding Ki-67 and RepoMan.
source: Thus, only in PP1γ is this pocket ordered and readily available for binding, which allows for the isoform specific interaction of Ki-67 and RepoMan.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural and biochemical data showing the role of R20 in ordering the L1 loop.

claim: GFP-PP1γ is enriched at anaphase chromosomes while GFP-PP1α shows a more diffuse distribution.
source: Transiently expressed GFP-PP1γ was enriched at anaphase chromosomes (Figure 2C,D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1). In contrast, GFP-PP1α showed a more diffuse distribution.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Changing residue 20 in either PP1γ (PP1γR20Q) or PP1α (PP1αQ20R) reverses the localization pattern at anaphase chromosomes.
source: Changing this single residue in either PP1γ (PP1γR20Q) or PP1α (PP1αQ20R) reversed this localization (Figure 2C,D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: GFP-PP1γ and GFP-PP1αQ20R bind endogenous Ki-67 in prometaphase-arrested cells, while GFP-PP1α and GFP-PP1γR20Q bind much more weakly.
source: GFP-traps showed that GFP-PP1γ and GFP-PP1αQ20R bind endogenous Ki-67 in prometaphase-arrested cells, while GFP-PP1α and GFP-PP1γR20Q bind much more weakly (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by GFP-trap experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: GFP-PP1γ, GFP-PP1β and GFP-PP1αQ20R bind both endogenous and ectopically expressed RepoMan in prometaphase-arrested cells, while GFP-PP1α, GFP-PP1γR20Q and GFP-PP1βR19Q bind much more weakly.
source: Similar GFP-traps showed that GFP-PP1γ, GFP-PP1β and GFP-PP1αQ20R bind both endogenous and ectopically expressed RepoMan in prometaphase-arrested cells, while GFP-PP1α, GFP-PP1γR20Q and GFP-PP1βR19Q bind much more weakly (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by GFP-trap experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A GFP:LacI fusion of Ki-67301-700 wt results in the recruitment of co-expressed RFP-PP1γ to a LacO array integrated at a single locus in DT40 chicken cells.
source: Similarly, tethering experiments showed that a GFP:LacI fusion of Ki-67301-700 wt or RepoMan wt results in the recruitment of co-expressed RFP-PP1γ to a LacO array that is integrated at a single locus in DT40 chicken cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by tethering experimental data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: RFP-PP1γR20Q fails to localize to the LacO array when co-expressed with GFP:LacI:Ki-67 or GFP:LacI:RepoMan.
source: In contrast, RFP-PP1γR20Q fails to localize, demonstrating it no longer binds Ki-67 and RepoMan (Figure 2F,G, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by tethering experimental data shown in Figure 2F,G and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The R20Q mutation abolishes PP1γ localization as effectively as mutating the canonical RVxF motif in RepoMan to RATA.
source: Remarkably, the R20Q mutation abolishes PP1γ localization as effectively as mutating the canonical RVxF motif in RepoMan to RATA.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of tethering experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The isoform specificity of Ki-67 and RepoMan is defined by a single residue in the PP1 catalytic domain, R20/Q20 (γ/α), not by residues in the PP1 C-terminus.
source: Together, these data reveal that the isoform specificity of Ki-67 and RepoMan is not defined by residues in the PP1 C-terminus, but instead by a single residue in the PP1 catalytic domain, R20/Q20 (γ/α).
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined structural, biochemical, and cell biological data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Regulator-specific isoform selectivity is achieved not only through interactions with the C-terminus, but also through interactions with the structured catalytic domain.
source: This is a fundamental result, as it demonstrates that regulator-specific isoform selectively is not only achieved through interactions with the C-terminus, but also through interactions with the structured catalytic domain.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing that R20 in the catalytic domain determines isoform specificity.

claim: The bulk of PP1γ relocalizes to chromosomes at anaphase onset.
source: Unlike PP1α, the localization of PP1γ changes dramatically during mitosis, with the bulk of PP1γ relocalizing to chromosomes at anaphase onset.
evidence: This claim is supported by the microscopy data and citations to previous work.

claim: PP1γ relocalization to chromosomes at anaphase onset is dependent on its ability to bind effectively to Ki-67 and RepoMan.
source: This relocalization is dependent on its ability to bind effectively to Ki-67 and RepoMan (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2003; Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2001) and is regulated by phosphorylation (Figure 3A) (Vagnarelli et al., 2006; Qian et al., 2013; Vagnarelli et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 2C and citations to previous work (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2003; Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2001).

claim: PP1γ relocalization to chromosomes is regulated by phosphorylation.
source: This relocalization is dependent on its ability to bind effectively to Ki-67 and RepoMan (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2003; Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2001) and is regulated by phosphorylation (Figure 3A) (Vagnarelli et al., 2006; Qian et al., 2013; Vagnarelli et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Vagnarelli et al., 2006; Qian et al., 2013; Vagnarelli et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2015) and data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: RepoMan S400, T412 and T419 are phosphorylated by CDK1-cyclin B.
source: For example, RepoMan S400, T412 and T419 are phosphorylated by CDK1-cyclin B (Vagnarelli et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Vagnarelli et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2015).

claim: Mutating RepoMan S400, T412 and T419 to phosphomimetics inhibits PP1γ binding.
source: Mutating these residues to phosphomimetics inhibits PP1γ binding, as evidenced by the inability of EGFP-RepoMan3D to pull-down PP1γ from non-synchronized HEK293T cells [see Figure 3F in Qian et al. (2015)] and an inability of RFP-PP1γ to localize to the LacO locus when co-expressed with GFP:LacI-RepoMan3D (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from Qian et al. (2015) and tethering data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: S507Ki-67 and T394RM have been identified as phosphorylation sites in proteomic screens.
source: Notably, the identity of the kinase that phosphorylates the S507Ki-67 and T394RM sites, both of which have been identified in proteomic screens (Dephoure et al., 2008; Nousiainen et al., 2006), has remained elusive.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to proteomic studies (Dephoure et al., 2008; Nousiainen et al., 2006).

claim: Aurora B kinase is redistributed from centromeres to the spindle midzone at anaphase onset.
source: Because Aurora B kinase is redistributed from centromeres to the spindle midzone at anaphase onset and because the S507Ki-67 and T394RM sequences match canonical Aurora B kinase phosphorylation motifs (Kettenbach et al., 2011), we reasoned that these residues are phosphorylated by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Aurora B kinase localization during mitosis.

claim: The S507Ki-67 and T394RM sequences match canonical Aurora B kinase phosphorylation motifs.
source: Because Aurora B kinase is redistributed from centromeres to the spindle midzone at anaphase onset and because the S507Ki-67 and T394RM sequences match canonical Aurora B kinase phosphorylation motifs (Kettenbach et al., 2011), we reasoned that these residues are phosphorylated by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on Aurora B phosphorylation motifs (Kettenbach et al., 2011).

claim: Both S507Ki-67 and T394RM are phosphorylated directly by Aurora B kinase.
source: Using in vitro phosphorylation assays coupled with NMR spectroscopy and mass spectrometry, we showed that both S507Ki-67 and T394RM (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) are phosphorylated directly by Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro phosphorylation assays, NMR spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutating S507Ki-67 to a phosphorylation mimetic (Ki-67496-536S507D) profoundly weakens the interaction with PP1 (~25-fold reduction in affinity).
source: Furthermore, mutating S507Ki-67 and T394RM to a phosphorylation mimetic (Ki-67496-536S507D/RepoMan348-450T394D) profoundly weakens their interactions with PP1 (~25-30-fold reduction in affinity; Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1.

claim: Mutating T394RM to a phosphorylation mimetic (RepoMan348-450T394D) profoundly weakens the interaction with PP1 (~30-fold reduction in affinity).
source: Furthermore, mutating S507Ki-67 and T394RM to a phosphorylation mimetic (Ki-67496-536S507D/RepoMan348-450T394D) profoundly weakens their interactions with PP1 (~25-30-fold reduction in affinity; Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1.

claim: The expression of GFP-LacI-RepoManT394D results in a significant reduction of the recruitment of RFP-PP1γ to the LacO locus.
source: Finally, the expression of GFP-LacI-RepoManT394D results in a significant reduction of the recruitment of RFP-PP1γ to the LacO locus (Figure 3B), i.e., to a level that is nearly identical to that observed for GFP-LacI-RepoManRATA and GFP-LacI-RepoMan3D.
evidence: This claim is supported by tethering experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Phosphorylation by Aurora B kinase in (pro)metaphase inhibits PP1γ binding to Ki-67 and RepoMan.
source: These data demonstrate that phosphorylation by Aurora B kinase in (pro)metaphase inhibits PP1γ binding to Ki-67 and RepoMan and, as a consequence, significantly contributes to prevent their premature recruitment to chromosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined data from phosphorylation assays, ITC measurements, and tethering experiments.

claim: Aurora B phosphorylation of Ki-67 and RepoMan significantly contributes to prevent their premature recruitment to chromosomes.
source: These data demonstrate that phosphorylation by Aurora B kinase in (pro)metaphase inhibits PP1γ binding to Ki-67 and RepoMan and, as a consequence, significantly contributes to prevent their premature recruitment to chromosomes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing that phosphorylation inhibits PP1 binding and the known timing of Aurora B activity.

claim: The phosphorylation of RepoMan at three distinct sites (S400, S412 and S419) by Cdk1 inhibits PP1 binding through a mechanism similar to Aurora B kinase inhibition.
source: Our data now explains why the phosphorylation of RepoMan at three distinct sites (S400, S412 and S419) by Cdk1 inhibits PP1 binding (Qian et al., 2015). Namely, it is similar to the mechanism by which Aurora B kinase inhibits Ki-67:PP1 and RepoMan:PP1 holoenzyme formation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural data showing that these residues are part of the PP1 interaction motif.

claim: All three CDK1 phosphorylation sites (S400, S412, S419), like the Aurora B targets S507Ki-67 and T394RM, are part of the PP1 interaction motif.
source: All three residues, like the Aurora B targets S507Ki-67 and T394RM, are part of the PP1 interaction motif and their phosphorylation blocks the interaction with PP1, which, in turn, prevents the premature targeting of PP1 to chromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the structural data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Phosphorylation of RepoMan at S400, S412, and S419 blocks the interaction with PP1, which prevents the premature targeting of PP1 to chromatin.
source: All three residues, like the Aurora B targets S507Ki-67 and T394RM, are part of the PP1 interaction motif and their phosphorylation blocks the interaction with PP1, which, in turn, prevents the premature targeting of PP1 to chromatin.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data on phosphorylation effects on PP1 binding.

claim: The premature targeting of PP1 to chromosomes leads to an increase in chromosome misalignment and a weakened spindle assembly checkpoint.
source: This regulation of holoenzyme assembly is critical as the premature targeting of PP1 to chromosomes leads to an increase in chromosome misalignment and a weakened spindle assembly checkpoint (Qian et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research (Qian et al., 2015).

claim: The expression of a PP1-binding mutant of RepoMan in HeLa cells results in extensive cell death.
source: In contrast, the expression of a PP1-binding mutant of RepoMan in HeLa cells results in extensive cell death, demonstrating the importance of the RepoMan-PP1 interaction for cell viability (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006).

claim: The KiR-SLiM is present in just two regulators (Ki-67 and RepoMan).
source: Finally, since the KiR-SLiM is present in just two regulators, the newly discovered KiR-SLiM binding pocket defines a novel surface on PP1 that is targetable for the development of drugs that inhibit only 1% of the distinct PP1 holoenzymes in the cell (2 of ~200) (Hendrickx et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by the database search results presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: The KiR-SLiM binding pocket defines a novel surface on PP1 that is targetable for the development of drugs that inhibit only 1% of the distinct PP1 holoenzymes in the cell (2 of ~200).
source: Finally, since the KiR-SLiM is present in just two regulators, the newly discovered KiR-SLiM binding pocket defines a novel surface on PP1 that is targetable for the development of drugs that inhibit only 1% of the distinct PP1 holoenzymes in the cell (2 of ~200) (Hendrickx et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing future therapeutic applications based on the structural findings.

claim: Both Ki-67 and RepoMan are highly upregulated in multiple cancers.
source: This is of profound interest because both Ki-67 and RepoMan are highly upregulated in multiple cancers (Dowsett et al., 2011; Vagnarelli, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Dowsett et al., 2011; Vagnarelli, 2014).

claim: The newly discovered LxVP SLiM substrate interaction surface is a well-known drug target site in the ser/thr phosphatase Calcineurin.
source: Targeting unique regulator binding pockets is a powerful approach as we recently discovered that the newly discovered LxVP SLiM substrate interaction surface is a well-known drug target site in the ser/thr phosphatase Calcineurin (Grigoriu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Grigoriu et al., 2013).

claim: More than 70% of PP1 regulators contain the RVxF SLiM.
source: This region includes the canonical RVxF SLiM that is critical for PP1 binding (505RVSF508, Ki-67; 392RVTF395, RepoMan; more than 70% of PP1 regulators contain the RVxF SLiM) (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PP1 regulators, supported by citations (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2006; Vagnarelli et al., 2011).

claim: Residues outside the RVxF motif are essential for PP1 holoenzyme formation and function.
source: Because recent efforts to understand how PP1 activity is directed by its >200 distinct regulators has revealed that residues outside the RVxF motif are also essential for PP1 holoenzyme formation and function (Peti et al., 2013; O'Connell et al., 2012; Terrak et al., 2004), we reasoned that this entire region was critical for PP1 binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Peti et al., 2013; O'Connell et al., 2012; Terrak et al., 2004).

claim: RepoMan is intrinsically disordered.
source: The lack of HN chemical shift dispersion demonstrates the lack of a hydrogen bond network in secondary structure elements and shows that RepoMan is intrinsically disordered.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 showing lack of chemical shift dispersion.

claim: Mutating F404 in RepoMan to alanine does not negatively affect RepoMan function.
source: Although F517Ki-67/F404RM are the most buried residues in both complexes, mutating this residue to an alanine does not negatively affect RepoMan function (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The Ki-67496-536:PP1γ7–308 holoenzyme crystal exhibits merohedral twinning with a twin fraction of 0.48.
source: The data was analyzed using phenix.xtriage and the intensity statistics suggested merohedral twinning (twin fraction of 0.48) with the space group of P61 and twin law h, -h-k, -l.
evidence: This is a technical detail about the crystallographic data analysis.
